reforms.description: Japan enacted comprehensive energy policy legislation in 1980 to address energy constraints through conservation and alternative energy development. The Alternative Energy Law (May 1980) established a new public corporation to lead technological development and commercialisation of alternative energy sources including coal liquefaction, geothermal, and solar energy, with provision of subsidies, debt guarantees, and loans. The 'Moonlight' project, a government R&D programme focused on energy conservation technologies, received substantial budget increases (over 150% to 8 billion Yen in FY 1980).
reforms.component_name: Alternative Energy Law and Public Corporation
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Energy conservation and alternative energy R&D reduce dependence on imported oil, lowering energy costs and improving allocative efficiency. Applied research in these sectors supports long-term productivity gains and technological capability.
reforms.status_evidence: Alternative Energy Law enacted May 1980; Moonlight project operational in FY 1980. Both legislative enactment and immediate implementation in same fiscal year.
reforms.importance_rationale: Structural, system-wide reform establishing new institutional framework (public corporation) and major budget increases for energy R&D in response to energy crisis. Combines legislative enactment with substantial funding commitment.
reforms.source_quote: The Alternative Energy Law, enacted in May 1980, calls for the MITI Minister to set and publish overall targets for oil substitution... A new public corporation is being established to play a central role in this area. Its main activities include: technological development related to coal liquefaction, geothermal and solar energy; granting of subsidies and debt guarantees for exploration of geothermal energy sources; and loans and debt guarantees for exploration of overseas coal resources.
